about: The database engine store, <data>/engines: one folder per engine version, and spawnloft-engine.json inside it saying what was installed. hasEngine compares the marker with this process, so Rust must write Node's platform and arch names (win32, darwin, linux; x64, arm64), never Rust's (windows, macos; x86_64, aarch64). test/contracts-files.test.mjs lays out a Garnet engine in a scratch data root with each marker and asks garnet.mjs hasEngine.

folders.note: mysql-<version>-<platform>-<arch> with Node names; garnet-<version> and mariadb-<version> have none

markers.text: JSON.stringify(value): one line, no spaces, no trailing newline

garnet.source: fs.writeFileSync(path.join(unpacked, 'spawnloft-engine.json'), JSON.stringify({ version, platform: process.platform, arch: process.arch, sha256: archive.sha256 }))
garnet.read: platform, arch and sha256 must all equal this process's and the pinned archive's, and the .NET runtime folder must exist

mysql.source: fs.writeFileSync(path.join(unpacked, 'spawnloft-engine.json'), JSON.stringify({ version, arch: process.arch, sha256: archive.sha256 }))
mysql.read: only sha256 is compared, with the archive for this platform and arch

mariadb.note: no marker: an engine is there when its server binary is

hasEngine.asserted: live where Garnet has a pinned archive for this machine
